metadata.note: The Buckfield Branch and its successors - the line from Mechanic Falls on the Atlantic & St. Lawrence (later Grand Trunk) north through Buckfield to Canton, extended to Rumford Falls, Livermore Falls, Rumford Junction on the Maine Central Back Road, and the Rangeley Lakes (Oquossoc, Kennebago); the Maine Central's Rangeley Branch after 1907. Drawn from research/branches/buckfield_branch_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-10-09; only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4: each era is its own operator and its own feature sharing geometry - Buckfield Branch RR 1850-56, Portland & Oxford Central 1862-72, Rumford Falls & Buckfield 1878-90, Portland & Rumford Falls Railway 1890-1907, Maine Central from the 1 May 1907 lease. The two total shutdowns (Oct 1856 - spring 1862, and 1873 - 15 Jul 1878) carried no traffic of any kind and are left as gaps. The one-month Portland & Rumford Falls RAILROAD lessee (Apr-May 1907) is not drawn; it is not known to have run trains.

source_conflicts: 1850 opening day: the 11th of January (Cole 1915; OCR reads 'nth') vs Tuesday 15 Jan (NH Gazette 22 Jan 1850, 'Tuesday last'). Same year either way.
Oct 1856 suspension: the 10th or 15th (Cole's OCR reads 'loth').

End of the Portland & Oxford Central: 'winter of 1872-3' (Bisbee, Oxford Democrat 1883) vs a court injunction of November 1873 (Cole) vs operations 'to 1873' (NCS/ICC). Drawn to 1872, the last confirmed year.
1878 reopening: trains 'on and after July 8th' (Portland Daily Press 26 Jun 1878 announcement) vs regular service from Monday 15 July (Cole; PDP 1883). Same year.

Rangeley line operator before 1900: NCS/ICC gives the Rumford Falls & Rangeley Lakes 'rail operations 1895-1899'; the P&RF's own 1903 advertisement sells the trains. Drawn as P&RF from 1900 (the first confirmed passenger year).
not_yet_sourced: OPEN START, portland-rumford-falls-canton-livermore-falls: drawn from 1900 (first passenger listing); the branch opened 1897 (Chisholm) / 1899 (Livermore Falls).
OPEN START, portland-rumford-falls-rumford-falls-chapman: drawn from 1900 (1900 Pathfinder); the Rangeley line was built from 1895.
OPEN START, portland-rumford-falls-chapman-bemis: drawn from 1902 (Sep 1902 timetable); Bemis may have been reached earlier.

OPEN END, maine-central-rangeley-branch-rumford-junction-canton: drawn to 1932 (Fowler 1932 letter); passengers ended 1933-1951, rails lifted 1952. Needs the date the Rumford trains were rerouted via Livermore Falls.

OPEN END, maine-central-rangeley-branch-canton-rumford and maine-central-livermore-falls-branch-canton-livermore-falls: drawn to 1954 (Fowler 1954 letter); the last Rumford passenger train is undated (MEC ended all passenger service 5 Sep 1960). Needs a Maine newspaper or ICC/PUC discontinuance record 1954-1960.
OPEN END, maine-central-rangeley-branch-rumford-oquossoc: drawn to 1932; abandoned after the March 1936 flood.
OPEN START AND END, maine-central-rangeley-branch-oquossoc-kennebago: drawn 1914-1933; opening year after 1907 unknown, and whether the 1933 railbus ran in 1934-35 is unknown.

Opening years 1892 (Canton - Rumford Falls) and 1893 (Rumford Jct - Mechanic Falls): drawn from 1894 (Fowler 1892-94 letters); an 1892-93 opening notice in the Portland Daily Press or Oxford Democrat would move both earlier.
Whether the P&RF owned and ran its own trains over Rumford Jct - Auburn - Lewiston 1893-1907 (Fowler line 2 headnote 'Rumford Jn-Lewiston ex Portland & Rumford Falls'). Not drawn.
Whether East Sumner - Canton (1871-72) carried regular passenger service at all; low confidence.

All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates except the 1863 twice-weekly P&OC service, the 1885-88 RF&B timetables (two trains a day, measured ~24 km/h) and the 1902-03 Rangeley line departures.
Not read directly: the ICC valuation report (via Nashua City Station only), Johnson 1985 and Jones 1980 (via Wikipedia only).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 13.3 mi against a documented 13.1 mi (MP 11.6 Mechanic Falls - 24.7 Buckfield; the 1849 mail contract says 12 mi). OSM MEC-tagged lifted grade throughout (roads, ITS 89 trail and unnamed abandoned ways on the old bed); the first 0.45 mi north of Mechanic Falls follows OHM way 201882645. Median deviation from the OHM trace 4 m, max 46 m. No straight-line leg, but the OSM grade is sparsely mapped in places: raw source vertices up to 1.8 km apart (south of Hartford) and 1.4 km (north of Mechanic Falls), drawn as the straight tangents the source gives. Buckfield end at the junction of OHM ways 201882645/201882637 (44.2897 N, -70.3669). ERA CAVEAT: this draws the grade as it stood before its 1952 lifting. The 1850s alignment may differ in places the research report flags - the 1855 bridge at Buckfield, the pond crossing beyond East Sumner (on piles, later drained and filled), and the 1869-70 Hartford - Canton track laid on frozen ground - and the 1850 junction with the Atlantic & St. Lawrence at Mechanic Falls is not known to coincide with the post-1893 one. Those differences are unmapped and not drawn.

segments.note: First train to Buckfield January 1850 (the 11th per Cole 1915, OCR-damaged; 'Tuesday last', i.e. 15 Jan, per the NH Gazette of 22 Jan 1850), hauled by the locomotive 'Pathfinder'. 5 ft 6 in Portland gauge, connecting with the Atlantic & St. Lawrence at Mechanic Falls. From 1851 F.O.J. Smith ran it as mortgagee in possession under the same name (not a Rule 4 split). Smith suspended the road in October 1856 (the 10th or 15th - Cole's OCR reads 'loth'), housed the rolling stock at Buckfield and closed the stations; nothing ran again until spring 1862. Some time before that (undated, 1855-56) landowners tore up the track near Mechanic Falls and mail and passengers were worked by hand cars round the break, then by stage - context only. Headway 720 (about two trains a day) is an estimate; no 1850s timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: Cole 1915 pp. 445-449 for the January 1850 opening and the October 1856 suspension; NH Gazette 22 Jan 1850; Fowler line 6 (1850 Pathfinder letters); NCS/ICC operations 1850-1856. Headway NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: Put back in service in spring 1862 by A.R. Morrill 'at a low rate of speed' (Cole), after five idle years; Smith's Portland & Oxford Central ran the trains (it bought the Buckfield Branch company 1 May 1863). The Worcester Spy of 20 Jun 1863 has trains running 'regularly, and as far as the town of Sumner, twice a week' - headway 5040 is that twice-weekly service; later frequency is not sourced. The road declined through the late 1860s ('in a sadly dilapidated condition', commissioners, Jan 1872). END: drawn to 1872, the last confirmed year (a train from Canton to Mechanic Falls in February 1872, Cole's annals). Trains were 'suspended altogether, in the winter of 1872-3' (Bisbee, Oxford Democrat 1883), while Cole has a court injunction stopping them in November 1873 and NCS/ICC gives operations to 1873 - running in 1873 is not established. Nothing ran again until 15 July 1878.
sources: Segment-level: Cole 1915 pp. 449-451 and the 1864 and 1872 annals; Oxford Democrat 1883 (Bisbee); Worcester Daily Spy 20 Jun 1863 ('twice a week'); railroad commissioners in the Portland Daily Press 15 Jan 1872 and 13 Jan 1873; NCS/ICC operations 1862-1873.

segments.note: LOW CONFIDENCE. Completed to Hartford December 1869; a train was run into Canton by 1 Jan 1870 over ties laid on frozen ground to meet a bond condition, but the track failed that spring (Cole) - a one-off, not counted as service. The railroad commissioners report Hartford - Canton (5 mi) opened during 1870 (Daily Kennebec Journal 4 Feb 1871), so 1871 is the first confirmed year; a Canton - Mechanic Falls train in February 1872 (Cole's annals) confirms 1872. Service was poor: Bisbee says trains 'did not run regularly', Smith tore down the Hartford depot and swore no train would stop there, and Canton sued in July 1873 for failure to run the road. It may have been intermittent mixed service. Headway 5040 (twice weekly) is carried over from 1863 and is an estimate here. END: drawn to 1872, the last confirmed year (a train from Canton to Mechanic Falls in February 1872, Cole's annals). Trains were 'suspended altogether, in the winter of 1872-3' (Bisbee, Oxford Democrat 1883), while Cole has a court injunction stopping them in November 1873 and NCS/ICC gives operations to 1873 - running in 1873 is not established. Nothing ran again until 15 July 1878.

Summer-only service to the Kennebago Lake sporting camps. START IS OPEN: the Maine Central extended the branch to Kennebago after 1907, year not given; Kennebago, Kamankeag, Realty and Cupsuptic first appear in the 1914 Guide (Fowler 'n'), so 1914 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start. END IS OPEN: Kennebago and Realty carry the 1932 letter, and the summer passenger trains were replaced in 1933 by a railbus built in the Sandy River & Rangeley Lakes shops (Jones 1980 p.298, via Wikipedia) - a railbus is rail passenger service, so 1933 is confirmed. Whether it ran in 1934-35 is unknown; the line was dismantled after the March 1936 flood. Do not extend either end without evidence. Headway 1440 (one summer train a day) is an estimate.
